title: VALSE: A Task-Independent Benchmark for Vision and Language Models Centered on Linguistic Phenomena

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing and balancing word and token frequency distributions between correct captions and foiled captions to ensure V&L models cannot solve the tasks by exploiting vocabulary imbalances.

Evaluating text-only unimodal models (e.g., GPT-1, GPT-2) by comparing perplexity scores of correct versus foiled captions to detect if models can identify foils simply because they are linguistically unnatural or implausible, independently of the visual input.

Constructing adversarial test sets (e.g., for counting tasks) where correct answers belong to infrequent classes (e.g., numbers >= 4) and foils belong to highly frequent classes (e.g., numbers 0-3), penalizing models that rely on frequency priors from the training data.
